problem: Households often struggle to coordinate daily meals, manage grocery lists, and assign cooking responsibilities, leading to repeated meals, food waste, and stress.
solution: A lightweight offline‑first web app that lets families create weekly meal plans, share grocery lists, assign cooking slots, and track pantry items, all stored locally in the browser.

competitors.name: MealBoard
competitors.difference: MealBoard is a paid SaaS with cloud sync; our app is free, offline‑first and stores data locally.

competitors.name: Cozi
competitors.difference: Cozi offers many family tools but requires sign‑up and ads; we provide a no‑login, ad‑free experience focused on meals.

features: Create a weekly meal grid with drag‑and‑drop meals
Add recipes or free‑form meal notes
Generate a consolidated grocery list from selected meals
Offline‑first with data saved in localStorage

monetization.pricing_hypothesis: Offer a premium export to PDF and optional cloud backup for $2.99/month after 1,000 active users.
monetization.free_tier: All core features remain free; premium adds PDF export and optional encrypted cloud sync.

operating_costs: Current prototype: ₹0 within published free‑tier limits
launch_strategy: Publish the site on GitHub Pages and share the link in family‑oriented subreddits and parenting Facebook groups.
Collect feedback via a simple in‑app survey stored in localStorage and iterate.
After 50 sign‑ups, add the optional premium export feature.

marketing_content.tagline: Plan meals, share chores, waste less – all in one free app.
marketing_content.social_post: Tired of the same dinner every night? 🍲 Meet FamilyMeal Planner – an offline‑first web app that lets you schedule weekly meals, assign cooking duties, and auto‑generate grocery lists. No login, no ads, just simple planning. Try it now at https://yourusername.github.io/familymeal-planner

tests: Add three meals to Monday, assign two different family members, generate grocery list – expect list to contain all ingredients from the three meals.
Open the app on a second device without internet, verify previously entered data persists via localStorage.
next_improvements: Add recipe import from public APIs (e.g., Spoonacular) with API key stored client‑side.
Implement optional encrypted cloud sync using a free backend like Firebase free tier.
Add push notifications for upcoming cooking assignments.
